title: Hans Peter Luhn and the Invention of Hashing (1953)
explainer: Python's dictionaries can look up a value by key almost instantly no matter how big they get, and that speed comes from hashing — an idea that traces back to a January 1953 internal IBM memo by researcher Hans Peter Luhn, who proposed scattering records across storage using a computed value instead of searching through them in order. That memo is generally credited as the origin of the hash table, now one of the most widely used data structures in computing and the thing a Python dict actually is under the hood.
